summary: Roomy mid-size electric SUV with a huge boot and Kia's class-leading 7-year warranty, priced to undercut most mid-size EV rivals.
pros: Largest boot in this comparison at 513L (1714L seats down)
Comfortable, family-friendly interior with strong rear-seat space
cons: Entry Air Standard Range is front-wheel drive only and rated to tow just 300kg braked
DC charging tops out lower than rivals, so road-trip top-ups take longer
Firmer low-speed ride than some competitors on Melbourne's rougher back streets

summary: Sharply priced small SUV from BYD with a well-equipped cabin and a strong warranty, aimed squarely at first-time EV buyers.
pros: Cheapest list price in this comparison at $39,990 before on-road costs
6-year/150,000km warranty with BYD's LFP Blade battery chemistry
Quirky but well-finished interior with a rotating touchscreen and good standard equipment
cons: Shortest range of the three at 345km WLTP on the entry Essential variant
Smallest boot of the comparison at 440L seats up
Resale value in Australia is still largely unproven for the brand

summary: Best-selling electric SUV globally, offering the longest range and lowest energy use of this trio plus access to Tesla's Supercharger network.
pros: Longest range in this comparison at 466km WLTP
Most efficient of the three at 13.9kWh/100km, lowering running costs
Direct access to Tesla's extensive Australian Supercharger network and frequent over-the-air updates
cons: Touchscreen-only controls, including for indicators and gear selection on some builds, split opinion
Comprehensive insurance premiums tend to run higher than the Kia or BYD due to repair costs
Braked towing capacity on the RWD variant is lower than the AWD Model Y variants
